headword: {新興住宅地|しんこうじゅうたくち}
reading: しんこうじゅうたくち
gloss: newly developed residential area; new housing development

definitions.gloss: newly developed residential area; new housing development
definitions.explanation: A residential area that has been newly built, typically on the outskirts of a city, with rows of modern houses and young families as residents.

examples.japanese: {新興住宅地|しんこうじゅうたくち}に{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: I live in a newly developed residential area.

examples.japanese: この{辺|あた}りは{新興住宅地|しんこうじゅうたくち}で、{若|わか}い{家族|かぞく}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: This area is a new housing development, and there are a lot of young families.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}から{車|くるま}で{十五分|じゅうごふん}ほどの{新興住宅地|しんこうじゅうたくち}に{家|いえ}を{建|た}てることにした。
examples.english: We decided to build a house in a new residential area about fifteen minutes by car from the station.

notes:
Composed of {新興|しんこう} (newly risen, emerging), {住宅|じゅうたく} (housing), and {地|ち} (area, ground). {新興住宅地|しんこうじゅうたくち} typically refers to suburban neighborhoods that were farmland or undeveloped land a generation or two ago and have been built up with rows of single-family houses. These areas are often characterized by similar-looking homes, young populations, new schools, and a relative lack of long-established shops.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新興住宅地|しんこうじゅうたくち}に{住|す}む: to live in a new housing development
- {新興住宅地|しんこうじゅうたくち}を{開発|かいはつ}する: to develop a new residential area
- {新興住宅地|しんこうじゅうたくち}が{広|ひろ}がる: new housing developments spread out

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {住宅街|じゅうたくがい}: residential district — any residential area, not necessarily new
- ニュータウン: new town — a large-scale planned residential development, often including commercial and public facilities
- {団地|だんち}: housing complex — a cluster of apartment buildings, often public housing
